directAnswer: Pope John XXI was Peter Juliani of Lisbon, the only Portuguese pope, who reigned from 8 September 1276 to 20 May 1277. A physician and scholar usually identified with the logician Peter of Spain, he died at Viterbo days after the ceiling of a room in the papal palace collapsed on him. A numbering error means there was never a Pope John XX.

paras: Peter was born in Lisbon and studied, according to most accounts, at Paris. He is generally identified with Petrus Hispanus, author of the Summulae logicales, a logic textbook used in European universities for centuries, and of the Thesaurus pauperum, a collection of medical remedies. Some modern scholars question whether all the works attributed to Peter of Spain are by the same man, so the identification is best described as traditional and widely held.
He served as a physician at the papal court, became archbishop-elect of Braga in Portugal, and was created cardinal bishop of Tusculum by Gregory X in 1273.

sections.h2: Why There Is No Pope John XX
paras: When Peter was elected at Viterbo in September 1276, he chose the name John. Medieval lists of popes had become confused, partly because some counted an antipope and partly through errors that suggested an extra John in the tenth or eleventh century. Believing there had already been twenty popes named John, he took the number twenty-one. The official numbering has never been corrected, so the sequence skips from John XIX to John XXI.

sections.h2: Bishop Tempier and the Condemnation of 1277
paras: In January 1277 John wrote to Bishop Étienne Tempier of Paris, asking him to investigate reports of errors being taught at the university. Tempier went further than an inquiry: on 7 March 1277 he condemned 219 propositions, many drawn from radical readings of Aristotle and his Arab commentators, and some touching positions associated with Thomas Aquinas.

Historians debate how far the pope intended this result, but the Paris condemnation became one of the most discussed events in the history of medieval thought. During John's short reign, the day-to-day direction of papal policy was largely in the hands of Cardinal Giovanni Gaetano Orsini, who would succeed him as Nicholas III.

John had a new apartment added to the papal palace at Viterbo, where he could study. In May 1277 part of the structure collapsed while he was inside. He was gravely injured and died several days later, on 20 May 1277. He was buried in the cathedral of Viterbo.
Dante, who admired his learning, places Pietro Ispano among the wise spirits in Paradise, praising his twelve books of logic. He remains the only pope from Portugal.

keyFacts: Born Peter Juliani in Lisbon; the only Portuguese pope
Traditionally identified as Peter of Spain, author of the Summulae logicales
Took the number XXI because of an error in counting earlier Johns
His inquiry led to Bishop Tempier's Paris condemnation of 219 propositions (1277)
Died at Viterbo on 20 May 1277 after a ceiling collapse

faqs.question: Why is there no Pope John XX?
faqs.answer: When Peter Juliani was elected in 1276, confused medieval lists led him to believe there had been twenty popes named John. He took the number XXI, and the numbering was never adjusted, so no pope bears the title John XX.

faqs.question: How did Pope John XXI die?
faqs.answer: Part of a new apartment he had built at the papal palace in Viterbo collapsed on him in May 1277. He died of his injuries several days later.

faqs.question: Was John XXI a scientist?
faqs.answer: He was a trained physician and is traditionally identified with Peter of Spain, who wrote a famous logic textbook and a medical handbook. Some scholars debate whether all those works come from the same author.
